chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ansari, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in a free Muslim woman performing salat (prayer) while her head is uncovered.

key_terms.الْحُرَّةِ: a free woman, not a bondwoman
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman referred to in the ruling
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: Can a free Muslim woman perform salat (prayer) with her head uncovered according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning the salat (prayer) of a free Muslim woman and states that there is no harm in her praying with her head uncovered. It is relevant to discussions in fiqh about prayer attire and the conditions of validity for women's salat.
